explanation: The clause 'or written' is false. Only creating the key is inside Try/Catch (ConfigurationStorage.vb 5-9); SetValue (14-16) has no handler, so a write failure on an existing key throws. At Main.vb 49 that is in Main_Load, and at 630-633 it lands in the Save handler's catch, which shows 'Saving failed' after the policy file was already written. Restate: only a key that cannot be created is silent; a failed write is not swallowed and can surface as a startup crash or a misleading save failure.

Same two harms are already carried by the settings-storage record (ConfigurationStorage 5-9) and the 'Saving reports Success' record (Main.vb 617-634). Merge or drop so one harm is told once at one severity. Also correct the settings half: only key creation is swallowed, not a write (SetValue 14-16 is unguarded).

Verbatim duplicate of the sibling record in the same subject on TLS 1.0/1.1 (Main.vb 19-20). Keep one; the stage must not tell one harm twice, and TLS is also told in at least five other records at different strengths ('may negotiate', 'code does not show an older version being used'). Pick one wording, state that Main.vb 20 sets exactly Tls|Tls11|Tls12 for the process (which also fixes the set to those three), and cite it once per subject.

Verbatim duplicate of the sibling record in the same subject on ownership change of a typed folder. One harm, told several times across the stage (also in 5 other records, with differing detail on 'any existing folder' vs 'for an administrator only' vs 'deletes for any user'). Keep one, and state the precise reach once: ownership and Administrators full control are applied only if isAdmin and the destination exists (94-100) or a language subfolder already exists (60-62); file deletion and ACL reset on moved files happen as stated in 64-73.

Verbatim duplicate of the sibling record in the same subject; drop one. And fix the claim in both: 'As administrator' is not what lists profile folders. OpenUserRegistry.vb 9-29 enumerates C:\Users for any user; administrator only changes the label (line 16). Mounting (PolicyLoader 62-78) enables backup/restore privileges and calls RegLoadKeyW whether or not elevated. Also 'C:\Users' is a hard-coded drive and the enumeration at line 9 is not inside a Try, so a Windows install on another drive throws when the dialog is shown.

Listing profile folders is done for any user, not only administrators (OpenUserRegistry.vb 9-29; line 8 only sets the access label). The hard-coded C:\Users at line 9 is unguarded, so on a machine whose profiles are elsewhere the dialog fails. Restate who can do what, and drop the duplicate record.

'That it is limited to administrator desktops is our assumption' contradicts the code and the sibling records: the manifest asks for highestAvailable (app.manifest 19), so the program starts for a standard user, and it tests writability and marks sources unmodifiable (PolicyLoader 54-60) and lets a non-administrator download (DownloadAdmx 55-63). Remove the sentence; say it runs for any user with the rights that user has. Also duplicates the other runs-where records; keep one.
Duplicate of the other purpose record, and its statement carries no cited lines in its basis. Keep one purpose record, cite README.md 1-12 and Main.vb 46-56 for the Home-edition download prompt.

Two clauses overreach. (1) 'only the ADMX/ADML files are moved': moveFilesInDir moves every file found at the top of the PolicyDefinitions folder and of the language folder (EnumerateFiles, 64-68), whatever its type. (2) 'the policy folder the app takes ownership of as administrator': ownership is taken only if isAdmin and the destination already exists (94-100); otherwise nothing is taken. Same wording about 'ADMX and ADML files' appears in the sibling no-hash record; correct both.

The edition check is not in the main window's load: it is in Main_Shown (Main.vb 46-50) and runs only while the 'CheckedPolicyDefinitions' flag is unset, i.e. on first run. The same sentence's other uses (Save in PolicyLoader 126) do run on every save; say so.

Reads more certain than its basis: nothing in the lines shows which runtime runs it or that 4.8 is installed, and the end-of-support date is not in the code. The README (30-35) says it targets Vista and Server 2008, where 4.8 cannot be installed. State only what the lines show (build target 4.5.2, config accepts v4.0 runtime with that sku) and mark the rest as outside the code, as the sibling record on this does.

'It still runs on newer 4.x runtimes' and 'receives no fixes' are not shown by the lines; same harm is told at three different strengths across the stage. Unify with the sibling .NET-support records and cite README.md 30-35 for the stated minimum.

'a later save can fail or be silently skipped' overstates the silence for hive loading. When the hive does not load, MainSourceRegKey is Nothing and the loader returns an empty PolFile marked not writable (PolicyLoader 71-74); the open reports 'cannot be saved' (Main.vb 320-330). The real harm is different: the person sees an empty source in place of the hive's policies with the load error code never reported (69). Privilege failures are ignored (Privilege.vb 8-13), correct. Restate both with their actual reach.

'No macros or conditional code are used' is contradicted by Settings.Designer.vb 26 and 43 (#If _MyType = "WindowsForms"), which the sibling build record cites. Say no custom conditional constants and no #If in hand-written code; the only #If is generated.
